title: P.3 Operations on Functions; Graphing Techniques

icans: I can combine functions and find the domain of the result.
I can form a composite function, find its domain, and write a function as a composition.
I can graph a function by shifting, reflecting, compressing, or stretching a basic graph.

vocab: y = f(x) + k moves the graph vertically; y = f(x − h) moves it _______________
y = −f(x) ___________ the graph about the x-axis; y = f(−x) reflects it about the y-axis

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Sum, difference, product, quotient: the domain is the numbers in the domains of both f and g; for f/g, also g(x) ≠ _______________.
Domain of f ∘ g: the numbers x in the domain of g for which g(x) is in the domain of _______________.

blocks.stem: f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = √(x − 1). Find f ∘ g and g ∘ f and the domain of each.

Find functions f and g so that f ∘ g = F.
a.  F(x) = (2x + 3)⁴
b.  F(x) = √(x² + 1)

notes: Shifts: y = f(x − h) + k shifts the graph of f right h units and _______________ k units (for h, k > 0).
Stretches: y = af(x) stretches the graph vertically when a > 1 and _______________ it when 0 < a < 1.

blocks.stem: Graph f(x) = (x − 1)³ + 2 starting from y = x³. Where does the point (0, 0) go?
Describe how to get G(x) = 2|x − 1| from y = |x|.

tickets.stem: Describe how to get y = √(x + 1) from y = √x.
